coverage.target: N/A — request-time performance, no infrastructure dimension. NFR1.1–NFR1.4 (200 ms budget, range-independent statement count, range-bounded series) are satisfied by the read module's single grouped local read and in-process fill (performance-design.md §1–§3). This stage provisions no compute, cache, replica or sizing tier to carry them; the only sizing-shaped quantity is the 10,000-row/365-day test fixture, which is a test instrument, not capacity to provision (infrastructure-specification.md §1 resource sizing, §5 no cache).

Infrastructure records the two posture-affecting facets: (a) NFR2.4 — the loopback bind is enforced at startup, the process-exposure boundary, recorded in infrastructure-specification.md §2.1 and §5 (no network boundary provisioned); (b) NFR2.2/NFR2.6 — no new egress path and no third declared runtime dependency, recorded in infrastructure-specification.md §1 (runtime dependencies capped at two) and §5 (nothing cloud/hosted provisioned). NFR2.1/NFR2.3/NFR2.5 have no infrastructure dimension (auth posture, parameter binding and credential handling are request-time code, and no secret store is provisioned).

infrastructure-specification.md §3 (no database/cache/queue service provisioned) and §4 (the shared SQLite file is existing infrastructure this unit reads through, not one it creates). The read-only guarantee (NFR3.1/NFR3.2) means this stage provisions no write path, no access-bookkeeping store and no mutating service; the only write to infrastructure is the startup schema migration, which is NFR4.5's concern.

Infrastructure records NFR4.5 (the additive, idempotent, atomic v3 → v4 migration with three named indexes) in infrastructure-specification.md §2.2 and §3. This is the unit's one genuine infrastructure-relevant change aside from the loopback enforcement: a schema change to the existing local SQLite file, committed whole or rolled back whole at startup. NFR4.1–NFR4.4, NFR4.6 and NFR4.7 have no infrastructure dimension (request-time failure shapes and per-section view degradation); recorded N/A with that justification in the reverse array.

N/A — invariant, not a target (no NFR5.y exists). Compatibility (/v1 freeze, envelope shape, SentimentClient interface unchanged) has no provisioned-resource dimension; this stage provisions nothing that could change it, and infrastructure-specification.md §1 records the run path and release artifact unchanged. Substantive mapping is BR4.7.

Infrastructure dimension is the dependency cap: infrastructure-specification.md §1 (runtime dependencies) and §5 (no new runtime dependency) record that C-6's exactly-two-runtime-dependency rule is unchanged by this unit, which is the infrastructure-facing half of maintainability. The remainder of NFR6 (module conventions, no junk-drawer, no new config) has no infrastructure dimension; the deployment surface here is one process and one file.

N/A — testability constrains how the instruments are built, not what infrastructure is provisioned. This stage designs no environment tier, no test infrastructure and no runner; the replaced concurrency harness and the test suite run under the existing local install (cicd-pipeline.md §4). Substantive mapping is BR6.6 and the team testing posture.

monitoring-design.md §1–§3: no monitoring tier is designed (C-5/C-6 forbid one; a localhost single-user app has no alerting channel and no monitoring subject), and what stands in its place is the module-logger failure records and the distinguishable error shapes already designed in NFR Design. The infrastructure-facing obligation is the recorded ABSENCE of any metrics/tracing/alerting/dashboard/SLO surface. NFR8.1–NFR8.3 land in the application log, not in a provisioned monitoring resource.

N/A — bounded-work scalability, no infrastructure dimension. NFR9.1–NFR9.4 (range-bounded series, limit-bounded payload, deliberately uncapped unbounded series, range-independent statement count) are properties of the read path, satisfied in process with no autoscaler, no replica, no shard and no queue to provision (scalability-design.md §3; infrastructure-specification.md §3 and §5 record every scaling resource as deliberately absent).
